messages.content: Predict a recorded valid allocation in a variable-exchange-rate dictator task. On this trial the participant divides the stated token budget between HOLD for self and PASS for the recipient. Each held token produces the stated hold-rate points for self; each passed token produces the stated pass-rate points for the recipient. Each point is worth USD0.10. Enter an integer number of tokens to HOLD from zero through the current budget. The passed amount equals budget minus held tokens. The original task entered hold and pass separately and repeated invalid totals; one valid joint allocation is one decision here. The recipient cannot accept or reject. There are20trials for each of two partners per TMS session,40choices in total, and two TMS sessions at least one day apart. Instructions and practice precede stimulation. Immediately before the task,40seconds of continuous theta-burst stimulation were delivered at rTPJ or the vertex control site; target order and partner-block order were counterbalanced. The minimally identified partner is a future participant displayed only by a subject number. The physically present partner is a previously unknown person introduced by name at the start, seated in another cubicle in the same room, with no interaction beyond that introduction. Their individual name, face and exact age are not recorded in these shared data and are not reconstructed. Choices are private. Only total payoffs from random selections are revealed at session end. One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Do not infer another person’s unobserved decisions. Output only the integer number of tokens HELD, with no explanation.

The minimally identified partner is a future participant displayed only by a subject number. Their individual name, face and exact age are not recorded in these shared data and are not reconstructed. Choices are private. Only total payoffs from random selections are revealed at session end. One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Do not infer another person’s unobserved decisions. Output only the integer number of tokens HELD, with no explanation.

One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Predict a recorded valid allocation in a variable-exchange-rate dictator task. On this trial the participant divides the stated token budget between HOLD for self and PASS for the recipient. Each held token produces the stated hold-rate points for self; each passed token produces the stated pass-rate points for the recipient. Each point is worth USD0.10. Enter an integer number of tokens to HOLD from zero through the current budget. The passed amount equals budget minus held tokens. The original task entered hold and pass separately and repeated invalid totals; one valid joint allocation is one decision here. The recipient cannot accept or reject. There are20trials for each of two partners per TMS session,40choices in total, and two TMS sessions at least one day apart. Instructions and practice precede stimulation. Immediately before the task,40seconds of continuous theta-burst stimulation were delivered at rTPJ or the vertex control site; target order and partner-block order were counterbalanced. The minimally identified partner is a future participant displayed only by a subject number. The physically present partner is a previously unknown person introduced by name at the start, seated in another cubicle in the same room, with no interaction beyond that introduction. Their individual name, face and exact age are not recorded in these shared data and are not reconstructed. Choices are private. Only total payoffs from random selections are revealed at session end. One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Do not infer another person’s unobserved decisions. Output only the integer number of tokens HELD, with no explanation.

Each held token produces the stated hold-rate points for self; each passed token produces the stated pass-rate points for the recipient. Each point is worth USD0.10. Enter an integer number of tokens to HOLD from zero through the current budget. The passed amount equals budget minus held tokens. The original task entered hold and pass separately and repeated invalid totals; one valid joint allocation is one decision here. The recipient cannot accept or reject. There are20trials for each of two partners per TMS session,40choices in total, and two TMS sessions at least one day apart. Instructions and practice precede stimulation. Immediately before the task,40seconds of continuous theta-burst stimulation were delivered at rTPJ or the vertex control site; target order and partner-block order were counterbalanced. The minimally identified partner is a future participant displayed only by a subject number. The physically present partner is a previously unknown person introduced by name at the start, seated in another cubicle in the same room, with no interaction beyond that introduction. Their individual name, face and exact age are not recorded in these shared data and are not reconstructed. Choices are private. Only total payoffs from random selections are revealed at session end. One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Do not infer another person’s unobserved decisions. Output only the integer number of tokens HELD, with no explanation.

The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Enter an integer number of tokens to HOLD from zero through the current budget. The passed amount equals budget minus held tokens. Immediately before the task,40seconds of continuous theta-burst stimulation were delivered at rTPJ or the vertex control site; target order and partner-block order were counterbalanced. The minimally identified partner is a future participant displayed only by a subject number. The physically present partner is a previously unknown person introduced by name at the start, seated in another cubicle in the same room, with no interaction beyond that introduction. Their individual name, face and exact age are not recorded in these shared data and are not reconstructed. Choices are private. Only total payoffs from random selections are revealed at session end. One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Do not infer another person’s unobserved decisions. Output only the integer number of tokens HELD, with no explanation.

Immediately before the task,40seconds of continuous theta-burst stimulation were delivered at rTPJ or the vertex control site; target order and partner-block order were counterbalanced. The minimally identified partner is a future participant displayed only by a subject number. The physically present partner is a previously unknown person introduced by name at the start, seated in another cubicle in the same room, with no interaction beyond that introduction. Their individual name, face and exact age are not recorded in these shared data and are not reconstructed. Choices are private. Only total payoffs from random selections are revealed at session end. One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Do not infer another person’s unobserved decisions. Output only the integer number of tokens HELD, with no explanation.

One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Predict a recorded valid allocation in a variable-exchange-rate dictator task. On this trial the participant divides the stated token budget between HOLD for self and PASS for the recipient. Each held token produces the stated hold-rate points for self; each passed token produces the stated pass-rate points for the recipient. Each point is worth USD0.10. Enter an integer number of tokens to HOLD from zero through the current budget. The passed amount equals budget minus held tokens. The original task entered hold and pass separately and repeated invalid totals; one valid joint allocation is one decision here. The recipient cannot accept or reject. There are20trials for each of two partners per TMS session,40choices in total, and two TMS sessions at least one day apart. Instructions and practice precede stimulation. Immediately before the task,40seconds of continuous theta-burst stimulation were delivered at rTPJ or the vertex control site; target order and partner-block order were counterbalanced. The minimally identified partner is a future participant displayed only by a subject number. The physically present partner is a previously unknown person introduced by name at the start, seated in another cubicle in the same room, with no interaction beyond that introduction. Their individual name, face and exact age are not recorded in these shared data and are not reconstructed. Choices are private. Only total payoffs from random selections are revealed at session end. One of the participant’s40choices is selected: self receives the kept money and that choice’s partner receives the passed money. The participant also receives the passed amount from a selected partner choice; the present partner receives their own held payoff from a selected prior choice, and their transfer enters the participant’s payoff if the selected participant choice was toward that present partner. Use only the supplied context and own past allocations. Where history or age is marked unavailable, it is omitted from these data, not necessarily unknown to the person. Do not infer another person’s unobserved decisions. Output only the integer number of tokens HELD, with no explanation.
